title: FIR-luminous [C II] Emitters in the ALMA-SCUBA-2 COSMOS Survey (AS2COSMOS): The Nature of Submillimeter Galaxies in a 10 Comoving Megaparsec-scale Structure at z ∼ 4.6
question: Investigate the star-formation activity, gas dynamics, dark matter halo masses, and environment of [C II]-emitting submillimeter galaxies at z ~ 4.6 in the COSMOS field.

recipe.goal: Search for emission lines in dirty cubes and assess completeness
recipe.method: Bin non-primary-beam-corrected dirty cubes to 80, 140, 300, and 750 km s^-1; subtract continuum using iterative 2-σ clipped channel average per pixel; divide each channel by its full-field rms to create SNR cubes; search for peaks with SNR > 6.2 and velocity-integrated SNR > 8; test completeness by injecting 1.2 x 10^7 simulated Gaussian lines into pure noise cubes.
key_parameters: Peak SNR threshold > 6.2; velocity-integrated SNR > 8 within ±0.5 FWHM
assumptions: Gaussian emission line profiles for completeness simulation

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux densities, line fluxes, velocity widths, sizes, and moment maps
recipe.method: Using primary-beam-corrected dirty cubes, re-calculate continuum excluding line channels to make line-free continuum maps and continuum-subtracted line cubes. Fit 2D Gaussians with CASA/imfit to measure continuum fluxes, velocity-integrated line fluxes, and beam-deconvolved sizes (for >3σ regions on moment 0 maps). Fit 1D Gaussians to spatially-integrated spectra for velocity widths and interpolate across spectral gaps. Generate moment 0 and moment 1 maps (with 3-σ clipping).
key_parameters: >3σ detection threshold on moment 0 maps for 2D Gaussian fitting and moment 1 clipping
assumptions: 2D Gaussian spatial profiles and 1D single Gaussian spectral profiles for flux interpolation

recipe.goal: Identify emission lines for unconfirmed candidates
recipe.method: Compare S_870µm / S_3GHz flux ratios with SMG SED templates as a redshift indicator, and compare observed-frame emission line equivalent widths (EW) with confirmed z ~ 4.4-4.6 [C II] emitters, intermediate-z high-J CO lines, and z ~ 9 [O III] lines.
assumptions: Typical SMG SEDs (Arp220, Cosmic Eyelash, composite SMGs)

recipe.method: Model foreground z = 0.73 cluster and nearby foreground galaxies (at z = 0.33 and z = 0.73) using a singular isothermal sphere (SIS) model. Convert galaxy stellar masses to velocity dispersion via the Faber-Jackson relation (for quiescent galaxy) or Tully-Fisher relation and σ^2 = V_rot^2 / 2 (for star-forming galaxy) to compute magnification µ.
assumptions: Singular isothermal sphere (SIS) profile; σ^2 = V^2 / 2; Faber-Jackson relation (Gallazzi et al. 2006); Tully-Fisher relation (Di Teodoro et al. 2016)

recipe.goal: Derive disk inclination, rotation velocity, dynamical mass, and dark matter halo masses
recipe.method: Calculate inclination i = cos^-1(a_min / a_maj) from deconvolved axes, and rotation velocity V_rot = (1/γ) * FWHM_[C II] / sin(i) with γ = 2. Estimate individual halo masses M_h^ind using an idealised spherical collapse model assuming V_rot equals the halo circular velocity. For close pairs (AS2COS0001.1/1.2 and AS2COS0034.1/34.2), also estimate lower-limit common halo masses M_h^NFW from projected separation and velocity offset assuming an NFW profile.
assumptions: Idealised spherical collapse model (Barkana & Loeb 2001); flat rotation curve V_rot equal to circular velocity of isothermal sphere host halo; thin circular disk geometry for inclination; NFW profile with c = 3.5; ΛCDM cosmology (Ω_M = 0.3, Ω_Λ = 0.7, H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1)

recipe.goal: Estimate duty cycle, [C II] luminosity function, baryon conversion efficiency, and cosmic SFRD contribution
recipe.method: Compute cumulative halo number density and [C II] luminosity function using survey volume 2.2 x 10^6 cMpc^3. Compare halo number density to Angulo et al. (2012) z = 4.6 halo mass function to infer duty cycle. Convert halo mass function to model [C II] luminosity functions using mean baryon accretion rate (Eq. 1), baryon conversion efficiencies ε = 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, and the De Looze et al. (2014) SFR-L_[C II] relation (Eq. 2). Calculate cosmic SFRD contribution from the two bright continuum-complete SMGs (S_870µm >= 6.2 mJy).
key_parameters: Full survey volume = 2.2 x 10^6 cMpc^3; baryon-to-dark matter ratio f_baryon ~ 1/6; ε = 0.01, 0.1, 1.0
assumptions: log SFR = -7.06 + 1.00 * log L_[C II] with 0.27 dex 1-σ dispersion (De Looze et al. 2014); baryon accretion rate formula from McBride et al. (2009); halo mass function from Angulo et al. (2012)

evidence.quote: From their estimated halo masses and [C ii] luminosity function, we suggest that these galaxies have a high (50–100%) duty cycle and high ( _∼_ 0 _._ 1) baryon conversion efficiency
We find that the 50–100% halos at _z_ = 4 _._ 6 with a mass of _M_ _h_ ≳ 4 _×_ 10 [12] M _⊙_ host SMGs.

We find that the model luminosity function with a baryon conversion efficiency of _ϵ_ _∼_ 0 _._ 1 agrees well with the observed luminosity function at least at the bright end (where our survey is likely complete).

evidence.quote: The contribution of the bright continuum-detected SMGs to the total SFRD is _≃_ 2 % at _z_ = 4 _._ 6.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes, CASA version (5.6.1), velocity binning widths, SNR thresholds, and analytic equations for halo mass, lensing, and baryon accretion are explicitly stated, and measurements are made directly on dirty cubes with CASA/imfit. However, low-level calibration/imaging parameters are delegated to Simpson et al. (2020), custom line-search scripts are not released, and exact channel integration windows and the M_dyn formula are unstated.
rediscovery_reason: All seven ALMA project codes are public, the line search and CASA/imfit measurement procedures on dirty cubes are straightforward and well-specified, and Table 1 provides a complete numeric answer key for all five sources.
